# Postmark — transactional email for Next.js Postmark sends an app's transactional email (welcome emails, password resets, receipts) with high delivery rates, bounce and spam processing, and detailed statistics. The official Node.js library `postmark` covers the whole Postmark REST API, uses the native Fetch API and has no runtime dependencies (Node 18+). ## Install ```bash npm install postmark ``` ## 1. Environment variables `.env.local`: ``` POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN=server_token_placeholder POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL=hello@example.com ``` The server token belongs to one Postmark server (Servers → API Tokens). The From address must be a confirmed sender signature or sit on a verified domain. ## 2. Create a client `src/lib/postmark.ts`: ```ts import { ServerClient } from "postmark"; export const postmark = new ServerClient(process.env.POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN!); ``` Use the client only in server code (route handlers, server actions, server components). Never expose the server token to the browser. ## 3. Send an email ```ts import { postmark } from "@/lib/postmark"; await postmark.sendEmail({ From: process.env.POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL!, To: "user@example.com", Subject: "Welcome!", HtmlBody: "

Thanks for signing up.

", TextBody: "Thanks for signing up.", MessageStream: "outbound", }); ``` `outbound` is the default transactional message stream. Keep transactional and broadcast email in separate streams. ## 4. Send with a template Create the template once in the Postmark dashboard, then send it by alias: ```ts await postmark.sendEmailWithTemplate({ From: process.env.POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL!, To: "user@example.com", TemplateAlias: "password-reset", TemplateModel: { name: "Ada", action_url: "https://example.com/reset?token=..." }, MessageStream: "outbound", }); ``` `TemplateId` (a number) works in place of `TemplateAlias`. ## 5. Handle errors `sendEmail` returns a promise that rejects with a typed error from `postmark`'s `Errors` export when Postmark refuses the message (inactive recipient, unconfirmed sender, invalid token). Catch it where the email is triggered so a failed email does not break the request that caused it. ## Why teams pick Postmark - Built for transactional email: high delivery rates, with bounce and spam handling included. - Templates live in the dashboard, so copy changes do not need a deploy. - Detailed delivery statistics and inbound email parsing come with the same account. # env files (can opt-in for committing if needed) .env* next-env.d.ts # Notely A small team notes app. Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind. ## Status - Users live in `src/lib/users.ts` as an in-memory list. - `/dashboard` shows the current user and the team. - There is no sign-in, no billing, and no email yet. ## Develop ```bash npm run dev ``` src/app/favicon.ico src/app/layout.tsx src/app/page.tsx src/app/globals.css src/app/dashboard/page.tsx

content.text:
Welcome and password-reset emails now go out through Postmark, wired into `src/lib/users.ts`. I haven't sent a real email, because I have no Postmark token. Lint passes. `tsc` reports one error, `LayoutProps` in `layout.tsx`, and it appears with my changes stashed too, so it was already there.

I chose Postmark because `docs/postmark.md` in the repo already describes it and it's built for transactional mail.

**Code**
- `src/lib/postmark.ts` creates the client the first time it's needed. If there's no token, the app still builds and runs.
- `src/lib/email.ts` has `sendWelcomeEmail` and `sendPasswordResetEmail`, with HTML and plain-text bodies and the user's name escaped. Sends never throw. A failure is logged, and if Postmark isn't configured the email is skipped with a warning. Either way the request that triggered it still succeeds.
- `src/lib/users.ts` gets three new functions:
  - **`createUser`:** rejects a duplicate email, adds the user, and sends the welcome email.
  - **`requestPasswordReset`:** creates a random token that expires after 1 hour and emails a link to `/reset-password?token=…`. It returns the same result whether or not the email exists, so callers can't use it to find out who has an account. Only a hash of the token is stored.
  - **`consumePasswordResetToken`:** accepts each token once and returns the user it belongs to.

**Config**
- `.env.example` has placeholders for `POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN` and `POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL`. I also added an optional `POSTMARK_MESSAGE_STREAM` and `APP_URL`, which sets the base URL in reset links.
- `.gitignore` ignored every `.env*` file, so I added an exception for `.env.example`.
- I added the `postmark` package and updated the README status line.

**Not built**
- Nothing calls `createUser` or `requestPasswordReset` yet, because the app has no signup form, API route or `/reset-password` page. The functions are ready for that work.
- There are no passwords yet, so `consumePasswordResetToken` only validates the token. Setting a new password has to come with the auth work.
- Users and reset tokens are in memory like the existing user list, so tokens are lost when the server restarts.

The email bodies are written in code, so changing the wording needs a deploy. Postmark's dashboard templates (section 4 of the docs) would avoid that if you want to switch.
